chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him) regarding the meaning of the two arbiters.

God abolished them, and through them strife emerged from the earth. One of them was more worthy of caliphate than the other, so God deprived them both of caliphate due to their excesses, and placed enmity and discord between them. One of them was more worthy of Imamate than the other, so God deprived them both of Imamate due to their excesses, and placed enmity and discord between them.

key_terms.الْحَكَمَيْنِ: The two arbiters (Amr ibn al-Aas and Abu Musa al-Ashari)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological significance of the two arbiters in Shia thought according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the arbitration of Amr ibn al-Aas and Abu Musa al-Ashari as a divinely ordained removal of their legitimacy, asserting that their mutual excesses led to the abolition of their authority. He highlights the irony that while one was deemed more worthy of caliphate and the other of Imamate, their actions resulted in fitnah, stripping them of both titles. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the arbitration was not merely a political compromise but a theological judgment on their suitability for leadership.

en.sayed-ali-raza: About the two arbiters (after the battle of Ṣiffīn)
